sections.html:
Two Lee County offices matter to a Fort Myers owner. The Lee County Property Appraiser sets the value, and the Lee County Tax Collector sends the bill and accepts the money.

For value, exemption or mailing address questions, go to leepa.org or call 239-533-6100. Payment questions go to the tax collector at 239-533-6000. The authorities that levy a tax are listed on your bill, and they are the ones to ask about ad valorem taxes and non-ad valorem assessments.

Payment opens November 1, and the full amount is due March 31 of the following year.

November payers get the biggest early-payment discount, 4 percent. It falls to 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February. A balance still open April 1 falls under delinquent-tax law.

The Lee County tax collector accepts payment six ways.

  • Online through its pay site, with a printable receipt.
  • Kiosks at any of six service centers, by card or e-check; e-check payments are free.
  • Secure SmartLockers at the downtown Fort Myers, South Fort Myers, Cape Coral and Lehigh Acres centers, open around the clock. The Bonita Springs center takes drop-offs inside during business hours. Allow five business days.
  • By phone at 239-533-6000.
  • By mail, following the instructions on the bill.
  • In person at a service center.

Payments are processed within two business days of receipt. The account history online shows PAID or UNPAID.

Lee County offers three ways to spread out or postpone a bill, and each has its own rules.

Lee County payment plans
PlanMain terms
Installment planApply November 1 to April 30; taxes over $100 per notice; four payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with discounts of 6, 4.5 and 3 percent on the first three
Partial payment planOpen to the current year; up to five payments an account; no discount; not taken online, and not for delinquent bills
Homestead deferralApply by March 31; age, income and lien limits; fire insurance naming the tax collector

Applications for the 2027 tax year run from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027. If the property sells mid-plan, the new owner has to carry the plan through for that year.

If the first installment is not in by July 31, you drop out of the plan, the tax notice is mailed by November 1 and you must reapply next year.

  • A missed second or third payment rolls into the next installment.
  • Any missed installment forfeits the discount.
  • The first payment is one quarter of the prior year's gross tax, and later payments may include half of any adjustment to current taxes.
  • Once enrolled and paid, you do not reapply yearly as long as the first installment is made each year.

Whatever is unpaid on April 1 is handled under delinquent-tax law.

Amendment 3 does not change the 2026 bill, which is due by March 31, 2027. The amendment takes effect January 1, 2027, and any resulting changes would show on next year's bills. Ask the Lee County Property Appraiser how it affects your exemptions or assessment.

The TRIM notice (Form DR-474) arrives in August and shows proposed taxes. Taxing authorities hold public hearings in September and October on tentative budgets and millage, then in October and November on final budgets and rates.

The tax bill itself comes in November. To challenge a value, file with the clerk within 25 days of the notice. If the August notice holds a surprise, you have time to check your exemptions with the Lee County Property Appraiser before the bill is mailed.

Save Our Homes holds a homestead's yearly increase to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower, and the state chart prints 2.9 percent for 2025. Other property can rise 10 percent a year.

The appraiser's home page has video guides on the homestead exemption and portability, on the non-homestead assessment limitation and on estimating property taxes. Give them a few minutes before you sell or buy, because a sale lifts the property to just value and the cap starts over.

The exemption removes up to $50,000 of value in two layers. The first $25,000 reduces every levy, school taxes included. The second layer, up to another $25,000, applies above $50,000 of assessed value and spares only non-school levies.

  • Apply on Form DR-501 with the appraiser by March 1.
  • You must live there permanently as of January 1.
  • It ends if the unit is rented, stops being your permanent home or you stop being a Florida resident.
  • Older, disabled and military owners may have extra relief; ask the appraiser.

The whole year's bill goes to the owner of record, and the closing agent works out each side's share.

A change of ownership is recorded with the Clerk of Court and then passed to the appraiser, so a seller may still get a bill because of timing. A mortgage company that no longer holds your loan can still appear on the notice, so confirm that no escrow money is left over. The next owner applies for their own homestead by March 1.

To prepare, gather your deed, ID and latest tax bill, and give the title agent the collector's payoff figure. Review the draft settlement statement a few days before closing. A cash buyer skips loan underwriting, which can shorten the schedule.

Taxes open on April 1 are delinquent. By June 1 the tax collector sells a certificate on the parcel to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate, bidding down in quarter-percent steps.

  • The certificate holder cannot press the owner for two years after that April 1.
  • After that the holder can seek a tax deed, paying a $75 application fee.
  • The clerk runs the auction, and the top bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger.

Selling before any of this happens keeps the payoff at closing simple.

Furniture, appliances and similar tangible personal property used in a home's rental activity can bring a separate tangible tax bill from the Lee tax collector.

If you recently bought a home that is no longer rented, call the property appraiser's tangible office at 239-533-6140. Renting out a homestead can also end the exemption under state rules.

faqs.q: How do I pay Lee County tax on a Fort Myers home?
faqs.a: Pay the Lee County Tax Collector online, by phone at 239-533-6000, by mail, or at a service center. Six service centers have kiosks.
Call 239-533-6100, the appraiser's number. Exemptions, values and mailing addresses are handled there.

faqs.q: When does the installment plan application close?
faqs.a: It closes April 30 of the tax year, and applications for 2027 taxes opened November 1, 2026. The first payment is due by June 30.

faqs.q: Why did I get a bill after selling?
faqs.a: The roll lists the owner of record when bills go out, and a recent sale may not have reached the appraiser yet. Pass the bill to the buyer or closing agent.

faqs.q: Can I pay delinquent Fort Myers taxes by check?
faqs.a: Not by personal check or eCheck. Ask the collector which payment forms it accepts for delinquent real estate taxes.
